requirements.requirement: The appworker account exists on node1
requirements.summary: useradd succeeded and id appworker returned uid=1000(appworker) gid=1000(appworker) pre-restart; post-restart id appworker confirmed the same identity.

requirements.requirement: appworker login sessions are limited to 8,192 open files
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft and hard nofile to 8192. Live verification via sudo -u appworker ulimit -n returned 8192 both before and after the reboot.

requirements.requirement: appworker login sessions are limited to 256 processes
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft and hard nproc to 256. Live verification via sudo -u appworker ulimit -u returned 256 both before and after the reboot.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes are fully satisfied. The appworker account was created (uid=1000), and /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf correctly sets both soft and hard limits of 8,192 open files and 256 processes. Live ulimit readings confirmed the limits apply to actual appworker sessions. The node-restart evidence protocol is complete and coherent: pre-restart boot identity (19062a82…) and healthy sshd baseline were captured, a reboot was issued and evidenced by two connection timeouts, a different post-restart boot identity (2d78c3ab…) was confirmed by both executor commands and the global after_executor snapshot, and post-restart verification confirmed sshd active, the account intact, and limits unchanged.
limitations: The ulimit verification used sudo -u appworker rather than an actual SSH login session; in practice pam_limits.so behavior for interactive logins may differ, though the limits.d configuration file is the standard PAM mechanism and the observed ulimit values match expectations.
The after_executor boot-identity snapshot (global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity) confirms the new boot ID independently, providing strong cross-check; no contradictions were found.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor state-changing commands had clear, task-required or protocol-required roles. cmd-00f95817a80945fe (useradd) and cmd-db11d80463fd4d4f (limits.d conf write) directly satisfy the task. cmd-55a9bd8fcafb4d17 (shutdown -r now) fulfills the node-restart evidence protocol. All other commands were read-only discovery or verification. No unnecessary mutations, no residue, no failed services, and package health remained clean as confirmed by the after_executor lifecycle snapshot.
